name: Natural recovery / monitored natural attenuation
mechanism: No active intervention; weathering, biodegradation and physical removal act over time
secondary_impacts: Oil persists longer where energy is low; monitoring effort only

name: Manual oil and oiled-material removal
mechanism: Hand tools and crews remove surface oil and oiled debris
secondary_impacts: Trampling and foot traffic can damage soft sediment and vegetation

name: Passive sorbent booms and pads
mechanism: Sorbent materials passively collect mobile surface oil
secondary_impacts: Sorbent waste generation; limited to mobile oil

name: Vacuum removal
mechanism: Vacuum equipment lifts pooled or mobile oil from the surface
secondary_impacts: Access and equipment disturbance; removes free oil only

name: Low-pressure flushing
mechanism: Low-pressure water mobilises surface oil to collection points
secondary_impacts: Can drive oil into sediment if misapplied; mobilised oil must be recovered

name: Low-pressure heated flushing
mechanism: Warm low-pressure water loosens more viscous surface oil
secondary_impacts: Heat harms sensitive biota; excluded on wetlands

name: High-pressure washing
mechanism: High-pressure water removes adhered oil from firm surfaces
secondary_impacts: High disturbance; drives oil down if used on soft substrate

name: High-pressure heated washing
mechanism: Hot high-pressure water removes weathered adhered oil
secondary_impacts: Hot-water washing initially worsened recovery at Exxon Valdez sites (NOAA OR&R)
source: NOAA OR&R / Exxon Valdez shoreline treatment studies

name: Surface-washing agents
mechanism: Chemical agents lift oil from surfaces for recovery
secondary_impacts: Chemical residue and mobilised-oil recovery concerns

name: Solidifiers
mechanism: Agents gel liquid oil into a collectable solid
secondary_impacts: Added material and waste; limited field evidence

name: Mechanical removal
mechanism: Heavy machinery removes oiled sediment and debris
secondary_impacts: Sediment loss and habitat damage; excluded on marsh and mudflat

name: Sediment relocation / surf washing
mechanism: Oiled sediment is moved to the high-energy zone for natural washing
secondary_impacts: Redistributes oil; only on exposed beaches

name: Sediment mixing / tilling
mechanism: Oiled sediment is tilled to expose oil to weathering
secondary_impacts: Can bury or spread oil; not for soft or sensitive habitat

name: Bioremediation
mechanism: Nutrient addition or seeding enhances microbial oil degradation
secondary_impacts: Effectiveness depends on nutrients, oxygen and access; limited bioaugmentation evidence (NOAA)

name: Oiled vegetation cutting
mechanism: Oiled stems and leaves are cut to remove oil and aid regrowth
secondary_impacts: Removes biomass and can increase erosion; only where sensitivity is high
